summary: Sproat Mountain lookout above Arrowhead, south of Revelstoke: tent in 1940, present building assembled 1956, no longer a working lookout; restored by the ATV club.

facts.design: Lookout building on cement foundation blocks; the present building was flown in and assembled in 1956
facts.status_note: Standing and maintained by the Revelstoke ATV Club. No longer a working fire lookout.

access.note: Public motorized and hiking routes. The mountain opens to ATV traffic on July 15 each year, and the summit was not to be reached before July 15 in 2023 because of grizzly bear spring habitat.

visit.trail_note: Reached by an ATV trail from forest roads south of Revelstoke, with a hiking trail alongside. The club asks riders to have at least intermediate skills.

facts.agency: Recreation Sites and Trails BC; the Revelstoke ATV Club manages the trail and maintains the tower

events.note: A trail was constructed to the top of Mount Sproat in September 1939.
The first lookout station was a tent erected for the lookout man. It was not a tower.
A Forest Branch News Letter item, quoted by Canada Lookouts, reports an assistant ranger at Arrowhead attacked by a grizzly bear on August 9th while climbing to the lookout with supplies.
A prefabricated 8 ft by 8 ft lookout building and a cabin were bought for $600 and $400 and taken up by pack horse. The building was used until 1955.
The present building was flown up by helicopter and assembled by a Forest Service carpenter crew. Canada Lookouts and the 2014 Revelstoke Review both give 1956 for a permanent lookout.
A road was completed to the tower for four-by-four vehicles only.
The club history says the Arrowhead Ranger District closed the lookout in 1968 because of flooding from the High Arrow Dam. The same history gives a later operating period, so see resolved_conflicts.
A January 1969 Squamish Times notice, quoted by Canada Lookouts, said there would be a lookout at Sproat Mountain part of the time.
Tourism Revelstoke says the Revelstoke ATV Club took over management of the lookout in agreement with Recreation Sites and Trails BC.
New stairs were installed, along with other repairs to the tower.
The tower was repainted, had new plywood laid on the floor, received information displays commissioned by Recreation Sites and Trails BC, and had the fire finder reinstalled.

corrections.why: The club history and Tourism Revelstoke describe a public motorized and hiking trail that opens to ATV traffic on July 15 each year, with a seasonal limit on the summit. They do not describe a closed site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The club history says the Arrowhead Ranger District managed the lookout until flooding from the High Arrow Dam closed it in 1968. The same history then says the Revelstoke Ranger District operated it from 1968 until it closed in the 1970s. The source contradicts itself. Canada Lookouts' January 1969 notice suggests part-time staffing that year. No other source read settles the date.
The 1940 tent and the 1956 permanent lookout do not conflict. The club history calls the 1940 station a tent, and the 1956 building is the first described as permanent.

notes_for_editor: Most dates rest on one club-written history (source 1, September 2023), which is partisan in tone. The 1956 permanent-lookout date is confirmed by Canada Lookouts and the 2014 Revelstoke Review. The Sites and Trails BC trail page REC2473 returned no text to fetch_text. Its search snippet calls the trail hiking only, which conflicts with the ATV club and Tourism pages. That snippet is not cited, so an editor should check the trail page. Sites and Trails page REC203929 also returned no text. The brief's Columbia Shuswap Regional District is not named in any fetched source, which places the lookout above Arrowhead and just south of Revelstoke, so the story leaves the district out. Brief access 'closed' is corrected to 'restricted'. Brief agency is expanded to name the club's management role. No elevation was found in the fetched text.
